## Overview

Uber ran through its entire 2026 budget for AI coding tools within months of the year starting, amid rising use of Claude Code, according to [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/05/26/uber-coo-ai-spending-tokens-claude-code/). By November, the company had responded not by cutting back on the tool but by centrally rewriting how it is configured for its engineers: automatic context compaction at 400,000 tokens, a medium reasoning-effort default instead of high, and a central gateway tha...

editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 source snapshots in full from the decompressed .html.gz files in sources/2026-11/uber-burned-through-its-2026-ai-budget-on-claude-code-then-rebuilt-defaults-around-compaction-and-medium-effort/ (source-0 through source-3), not just excerpts. source-0 (VentureBeat, Louis Columbus, Nov 19 2026): every direct quote in the article attributed to VentureBeat/Medisetty/Jeff Simon/Anjul Bhambhri is verbatim in the snapshot, including 'The engineer didn't pick any of those settings; Uber picked them,' 'cost a lot,' 'a good medium balance,' 'perform much better at medium effort level,' 'some degradation at high,' 'That didn't work at all,' 'going to get confused as it works through the plethora of documentation,' 'as narrow as possible,' 'very generic response,' 'the right context for the right task for the right person,' 'a mental map of how Uber works,' 'a very simple cache based on how customers commonly ask questions,' and 'real trend line.' Numeric figures (400,000-token compaction trigger; 700,000-800,000 token cache-miss threshold; one-hour/five-minute cache lifetimes; 50,000-70,000 token MCP tool-definition cost; ~34% cost-per-1,000-requests reduction from peak; 52% cost-per-session reduction from June peak; 90% feature-flag cleanup cost cut; ~200 million vs. 104 million (24M nodes/80M edges) context-graph size; the 38-second vs. 20:09 lookup example; the 9.4x agentic-request growth Feb-Aug; the 156-respondent/26%/44%/38% VB Pulse survey figures) all match the snapshot exactly and are correctly attributed to Uber/Medisetty/VentureBeat's survey, not claimed as the Herald's own calculation. source-1 (Fortune, Jake Angelo, May 26 2026): every quote attributed to Fortune is verbatim, including the 'burnt through its entire 2026 AI coding tools budget in just four months after incentivizing employees...leaderboard ranking teams by total AI tool usage' framing (word-for-word), Macdonald's 'That link is not there yet' / 'Maybe implicitly...25% more useful consumer features' / 'if you're not actually able to draw a direct line...that trade becomes harder to justify,' and Khosrowshahi's 'We're seeing uptake of these tools...' / 'We think it's creating employees with superpowers.' The 90%-cheaper-inference-by-2030 Gartner figure, the $207B/139%/$86.4B AI-agent-spending Gartner figure, and the ~10%-autonomous-agent-code figure all match the snapshot exactly, including the article's correct framing of the $207B figure as a 'separate' Gartner forecast from the 90%-inference one. source-2 (code.claude.com/docs/en/costs) and source-3 (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort): both quotes attributed to Anthropic's own documentation are verbatim — 'CLI tools...are still more context-efficient than MCP servers because they don't add any per-tool listing' (source-2) and medium effort as 'balanced approach with moderate token savings' suited to 'agentic tasks that require a balance of speed, cost, and performance,' with high effort as 'the default on most models that support it' (confirmed: the doc lists high as default on every model except Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5, i.e. most of the listed models) 'spends as many tokens as the task needs for excellent results' (source-3). These two vendor sources are used only for Rule 9 technical grounding on Claude's own cost/effort mechanics, never as sourcing for the Uber narrative itself — consistent with the writer's self-report. Independent-source count: 2 of 4 (VentureBeat and Fortune), both fully independent of Uber and of Anthropic; satisfies the Analysis-category minimum of 2 independent sources. Anthropic disclosure: required - Claude Code is central to the headline/lead and the article quotes Anthropic's own docs; the submission includes the required one-sentence disclosure ('Disclosure: the Herald's contributor model is built by Anthropic...') at the end of the Implications section.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated or misattributed claims found. Timeline is handled correctly and does not conflate the two reports: the article explicitly frames Fortune's reporting as 'late May' (Macdonald's ROI skepticism, the budget-exhaustion leaderboard story, Khosrowshahi's 10%-autonomous-code remark on 'an earnings call the same month') and VentureBeat's reporting as the 'November' follow-up (the AIFX wrapper, the four cost-control defaults, the October 28 summit remarks, the April CTO comment to The Information about exhaustion in 'the first few months of the year' — which is consistent with, not contradictory to, Fortune's 'four months' framing). The ~34%/~52% cost-reduction figures are explicitly presented as 'Uber reported' via VentureBeat, not as independently verified by the Herald — matches the raw source text, which likewise only reports Uber's self-measured figures with no independent verification by VentureBeat either. Derived figures: the article does not compute any new sums/ratios of its own from raw data; all figures are sourced and attributed. No disagreements between sources requiring reconciliation.
